claims.text: Adding trace yttrium to FeNiCoCrAl promotes yttrium segregation at the oxide/metal interface.
Yttrium segregation at the oxide/metal interface enhances adhesion of the protective Al2O3 scale.
Adding trace yttrium reduces oxide-scale spallation during high-temperature oxidation.
The unmodified FeNiCoCrAl alloy develops an Al2O3 scale during oxidation under the stated conditions.
Interfacially segregated yttrium lowers the oxide/metal interfacial energy.
Interfacially segregated yttrium modifies the adhesion properties of the growing Al2O3 layer.
The yttrium-induced interfacial process inhibits pore formation in the oxide scale.
Inhibiting pore formation and scale spallation produces a more uniform and adherent oxide layer.
A more uniform and adherent Al2O3 layer improves oxidation resistance.
After oxidation at 1050°C in air for 72 hours, the Y-modified alloy will have a more uniform, more adherent, and less spalled Al2O3 scale than the Y-free alloy.
Under the same oxidation conditions, Y-free FeNiCoCrAl is expected to form a less adherent and more defect-prone oxide scale.

The proposed mechanism is applicable to FeNiCoCrAl oxidized in air at 1050°C but may not generalize to other compositions, reactive-element additions, or substantially different oxidation environments.
